name: University of Porto (Rectorate)
short: The rectorate of the University of Porto on Praça de Gomes Teixeira, in a historic neoclassical building of 1807.
long: The University of Porto was founded on 22 March 1911, and its rectorate occupies a historic neoclassical building on Praça de Gomes Teixeira, known in the city as Praça dos Leões. The original design was drawn up by Carlos Amarante in 1807 for the Royal Academy of Navy and Commerce. Today, besides the rectorate, the building houses the Museum of Natural History and Science and the zoology, geology and archaeology museums.
history:
The University rests on two 19th-century higher schools: the Polytechnic Academy (1837), heir to the Royal Academy of Navy and Commerce of 1803, and the Medical-Surgical School (1836). Its more distant forebears include the Nautical Class established by José I in 1762 and the Drawing and Design Class created by Maria I in 1779.

The University of Porto was created by a decree of the Provisional Republican Government on 22 March 1911 and inaugurated on 16 July 1911; that same day the mathematician Francisco Gomes Teixeira was elected its first rector. The decree of 19 April 1911 set out its structure: a Faculty of Sciences (with the engineering chairs of the abolished Polytechnic Academy), a Faculty of Medicine with a school of pharmacy, and a Faculty of Commerce that never actually operated. A Technical Faculty followed in 1915 (renamed Faculty of Engineering in 1926), a Faculty of Letters in 1919 (closed in 1928, restored in 1961), a Faculty of Pharmacy in 1921 and a Faculty of Economics in 1953.

The historic rectorate building, rectangular and neoclassical, was intended for the Royal Academy of Navy and Commerce. The original project by Carlos Amarante dates from 1807. During the French invasions and the Liberal Wars construction advanced very slowly, and the unfinished building served as a hospital during the Siege of Porto (1832–1833). In 1833 the project was remodelled by J. C. Vitória Vila-Nova, followed by two further major rebuilds, in 1862 (Gustavo Gonçalves e Sousa) and 1898 (António Araújo e Silva).

The building has housed the Polytechnic Academy, the Colégio dos Órfãos, the Academy of Fine Arts, the National Lyceum, the Industrial Institute (forerunner of ISEP, until 1933), the Technical and then Engineering school (until 1937), the Faculty of Economics (until 1974) and the Faculty of Sciences (until 2007). It has twice caught fire: on 20 April 1974 a large fire destroyed much of it, and on 5 May 2008 the roof, then under restoration, caught fire; the blaze was brought under control at 12:55 and no one was hurt.

Today the historic building houses the rectorate of the University of Porto and the Museum of Natural History and Science, created in 2015 by merging the Natural History Museum and the Science Museum. In front of it, on Praça de Gomes Teixeira (Praça dos Leões), runs the Fonte dos Leões, the fountain of the lions; a few minutes away are the Cordoaria garden and the Clérigos tower.
facts: The university was founded by decree on 22 March 1911 and inaugurated on 16 July 1911.
The mathematician Francisco Gomes Teixeira was elected its first rector.
The rectorate building was begun to a design by Carlos Amarante in 1807.
During the Siege of Porto (1832–1833) the unfinished building served as a hospital.
It was rebuilt in 1862 and 1898 and survived major fires in 1974 and 2008.
The Faculty of Sciences occupied the building until 2007; it now houses the rectorate and the Museum of Natural History and Science.
The square in front is Praça de Gomes Teixeira, also known as Praça dos Leões, with its fountain of the lions.
tip: Admire the Fonte dos Leões, the fountain of the lions, on the square in front of the rectorate. The historic building also houses the Museum of Natural History and Science. The Clérigos tower and the Cordoaria garden are a few minutes’ walk away, so the visit fits easily into a walk through the Baixa.
